title: Jointly Predicting Courses and Grades Using a Transformer-Based Model
abstract: arXiv:2608.13409v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Existing predictive models in learning analytics often treat student academic history as a simple sequence, overlooking the concurrent nature of courses taken within a semester. This simplification can lead to inaccurate performance predictions, particularly for students with heavy or challenging course loads. This paper introduces a TRansformer for Academic Course-grade Estimation (TRACE) that addresses this limitation by jointly predicting both the set of courses a student will take and their corresponding grades for an upcoming semester. Our approach encodes courses on a per-semester basis to capture the effects of course concurrency and utilizes a novel loss function combining course-set prediction with grade prediction. We demonstrate that predicting courses taken in addition to the grades in those courses leads to significant improvements in prediction quality. translated_title: 基于Transformer模型的课程与成绩联合预测
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.13409v1 公告类型：新 摘要：学习分析中的现有预测模型通常将学生学术历史视为简单序列，忽略了同一学期内所修课程的并发性。这种简化可能导致性能预测不准确，尤其对于课程负担重或挑战性大的学生。本文介绍了一种用于学术课程成绩估计的Transformer模型（TRACE），通过联合预测学生即将修读的课程集合及其对应成绩来解决这一局限性。我们的方法按学期对课程进行编码，以捕捉课程并发效应，并利用一种新颖的损失函数，将课程集合预测与成绩预测相结合。我们证明，除了预测课程中的成绩外，预测所修课程能显著提升预测质量。基于十年机构数据训练，我们的联合预测模型实现了性能提升。
tldr: 本文提出TRACE模型，通过联合预测学生未来学期的课程集合和成绩，利用课程并发性信息，显著提高了学业成绩预测的准确性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces TRACE, a model that jointly predicts course sets and grades for upcoming semesters, leveraging course concurrency to significantly improve academic performance prediction accuracy.
